objects.original: Eq. (13)–(16) give actual radialized tensor-degree fields from one joint standard coefficient vector; their deterministic weighted sum is the random variable used in Eq. (51).
objects.reconstructed: A single Euclidean standard Gaussian vector is indexed by the disjoint union of ordered (level,degree) coefficient coordinates. Coordinate restriction and unscaled Euclidean packaging feed the literal angular contraction, evaluated on the normalized tail of the same x and multiplied by the exact cutoff, with zero extension.
objects.evidence: For each of the p copies of the order-S_i tensor, a slot (j,t) with t<K^j contributes u_j at the assigned coordinate. The product over all slots and sum against the same coefficients reproduce the entrywise inner product, scaled by sqrt(n)a_{i,p}. WithLp.toLp does not rescale; no coefficient is redrawn, symmetrized, or replaced by an arbitrary marginal.

domains.original: x lies in R^{(h+1)n}; i runs from 0 to h, p through {4,6,...,P}, and level i uses the blocks x_i,...,x_h; the (i,p) coefficient block is R^{n^{p S_i}}.
domains.reconstructed: x has h+1 Euclidean n-vectors; degrees are the even-at-least-four subtype of Fin(P+1). Each coefficient is an assignment of p copies of relative tail slots into Fin n.
domains.evidence: The relative index j in Fin(h-i+1) corresponds to the absolute index i+j, so the exponent is K^j=K^{(i+j)-i}; the slot count is p S_i and the assignment count is n^{p S_i}. The upper degree P is included. Positive n, finite h, and h=i with its single tail block are well-typed.

quantifiers.original: The paper constructs a large-n family with prescribed depth and Eq. (18) deterministic positive beta_i, then fixes one x before computing its coefficient expectation.
quantifiers.reconstructed: For all positive n, natural h, and deterministic real beta and x, one W is built on a single full coefficient draw with those same x and beta.
quantifiers.evidence: The paper's weights and prescribed depth specialize this finite identity. Only deterministic multiplication and finite Gaussian addition are used, so zero/negative weights and arbitrary finite depth cause no mathematical change in the isolated formula. This extension does not apply to admissibility or Eq. (18)'s estimates.

assumptions.original: The coefficients are independent standard Gaussian tensor blocks by construction; their original joint law is mu_n. The radial extension covers zero blocks.
assumptions.reconstructed: The measure is exactly stdGaussian on the full Euclidean coefficient space. All fields use the same coefficient point; there are no additional probabilistic or analytic premise binders.
assumptions.evidence: The actual joint product law is obtained by radialLevels_hasLaw at this x, not assumed. Cutoff zero and a zero tail block are permitted; chi(0)=0 so the variance formula remains valid there. The MGF and moment facts supply integrability and measurable-law requirements internally, without nondegeneracy, event, or regularity hypotheses.

conclusion.original: The paragraph before Eq. (51) gives centered Gaussian W with variance V=n sum_i beta_i^2 C_i(x)^2 v_i. Eq. (51) gives the finite expectation of exp(-W) as exp(V/2).
conclusion.reconstructed: HasLaw gives the exact pushforward gaussianReal 0 V.toNNReal, Integrable is a separate conclusion, and the displayed real integral equals exp(V/2).
conclusion.evidence: Gaussian scalar multiplication squares beta; variances add by independence, and the real V is a nonnegative sum of squares. Thus toNNReal preserves it. For V=0 the pushforward is dirac 0 and the mean of exp(-W) is one. The exact law gives mgf at -1; strict positivity plus the nonzero probability measure proves Integrable, so the real-integral equality cannot be a default-value artifact.

scopes.original: The calculation is the unconditional coefficient expectation of the linear weight at fixed x. It defines m(x), before the separate M and mass comparisons.
scopes.reconstructed: Only the coefficient vector is integrated, under its original law. No spatial integration, gate, energy truncation, good-event restriction, or conditioning enters the theorem.
scopes.evidence: Eq. (49) identifies the nonlinear weight with the linear one only on the good event; Eq. (51) has no such restriction and integrates exp(-W) itself. The module and the lesson keep this distinction and claim neither Eq. (52) first moments, any tilted law, nor a main lower bound.

constant_dependencies.original: The variance uses n, beta_i, C_i(x), v_i=sum_p a_{i,p}^2, with the exact K=2^{74(h+1)}, P=2^{64(h+1)}, S_i and Eq. (14) amplitude; footnote 2 and Eq. (16) fix the cutoff.
constant_dependencies.reconstructed: The same powers, relative tail lengths, amplitude denominator p^4 S_i^2 sqrt((h-i+1) log(2 P S_i)), squared weights and cutoff products, and literal variance factor n and exponent factor 1/2 appear.
constant_dependencies.evidence: The thresholds 13/20, 7/10, 19/20 and 1, with the exp(-1/t) glue for positive t and zero otherwise, equal the source's two quotient factors. The denominators are positive because the lower and upper ramp endpoints are strictly ordered. The decoder calls the upper degree Q and the tensor base R; these are not new parameters. No cutoff replacement, loose bound, or change of constant occurs.

deltas.description: Expand entrywise ordered tensor contraction and the original direct sum into finite assignment coordinates and one Euclidean standard Gaussian without rescaling.

The isolated finite formula permits arbitrary deterministic real beta and any positive n and natural h; the paper's prescribed parameters are a specialization, not a generalization of its admissibility or lower-bound results.
HasLaw and Integrable expose the exact pushforward, its variance-zero case, and finiteness already asserted by the source's displayed finite expectation.
